note: Educational demos made to show an open-source tool. Not research. Hand-made alignment of Wharton's Greek (lines 1-16) to six public-domain versions. Token ids point into results/versions.json.
scope: Greek lines 1-16 (four stanzas) as printed by Wharton

gloss.gloss: any one who, anything which, whosoever

gloss.form_note: Aeolic ἆδυ for ἡδύ, neuter used as adverb
κάτ before μ (κὰμ), split from its verb (κατέαγε)

gloss.gloss: forthwith, at once, in a moment

gloss.form_note: Aeolic ἀ (ἁ) for ἡ, the article
as printed by Wharton, μίδρως = μ' ἴδρως, 'sweat ... me'
Aeolic first person ἔμμι for εἰμί

gloss.gloss: in need or want of, lacking

gloss.form_note: in square brackets in Wharton's text: an editor's supplement

greek:9:2.note: κὰμ ... ἔαγε = 'broken down': Wharton keeps the prefix

gloss_source.lexicon: LSJ, A Greek-English Lexicon (9th ed., 1940), Perseus digital edition
